tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Gerhard Albersheim in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 8. Facsimile-Buch Mikulitsch gezeigt;Karl Lothar Mikulicz, Ein Notierungsbuch von Beethoven aus dem Besitze der Preussischen Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1927): a transcription of “Landsberg 7,” which contains sketches primarily for The Creatures of Prometheus, Op. 43, and the sonatas Op. 23, 24, and 26. aus Beethoven op. 10III Menuett: Tauschstelle.

10. Aus Nottebohms SkizzenbuchGustav Nottebohm, Ein Skizzenbuch von Beethoven aus dem Jahre 1803 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1880), with selective transcriptions from, and commentary on, “Landsberg 6,” commonly known as the “Eroica” Sketchbook. Skizzen zum 1. Satz, wie sie zu lesen sind.
22. Nachträgliche Erläuterungen; Eintragungen aus der rev. Abschr.; Vortrag im Großen.

26. Sommernachtstraum Ouvertüre:Diary Oct 23: “I work on the Overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream for Albersheim.” – An undated sketch for a graph of this work is preserved as part of OC 48/13. Bild der Urlinie, Entschleierung der letzten Geheimnisse der Parallelismen. A. bezeichnet den Besuch der Nilius-KurseRudolf Nilius (1883–1962), Austrian conductor and composer; diary Oct 26: “Albersheim already complains after the first lesson that Nilius is a waste of time for him.” – Diary Oct 15: “From 8:30 to 11, concert of the Philharmonic under Nilius ([broadcast] to the central European region): [...] – a refreshing evening, the tempos mainly correct, in spite of certain liberties taken in the dances.” The program was titled “Music from Austria” and included works by Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, and Johann Strauss the Elder and the Younger. als Zeitverlust.

5. XI. Wieder Durchsicht des 1. Satzes begonnen, Erläuterung einiger Stellen dazu.Diary Nov 5: “Albersheim attempts to make hasty progress on the symphony – not out of craving, more out of curiosity; I succeed in curbing this and summon him back to his obligation to precision.”

9. Marsch aus der Sommernachtstraum-Musik, Bild der Urlinie u. Vortrag.Diary Nov 7: “From Albersheim (postcard): he asks for the Wedding March by Mendelssohn, to be explained as early as midday; I write it out after lunch.”
Bemerkungen zu Hoesslins Vortrag von Brahms I. Sinfonie zu Berlioz Symphonie phantastique; Scherzo begonnen.
16. Bild des 4. Satzes. Fragen zu Schuberts Sinfonie Bdur.
26. Fragen zu Schuberts Rosamunde Ballett, Bd u. Gm-Stellen; zeige Hecks Skizzen zu Beethovens VI., letzter Satz.
30. Linie zu Schubert Cdur-Sinfonie, Andante, Fdur-Stelle; Linie zu Chopin Nocturne Fdur korrigirt; Linie Bach Toccata Fdur korrigirt.

3. XII. Mendelssohn „Die Liebende schreibt,“ Linie korrigirt;Diary Dec 1: “Work on Bach's Toccata and Mendelssohn's "Die Liebende schreibt" (for Albersheim).” -- The minuet, which is part of Schubert’s Piano Sonata in G major, D. 894, served as the principal case study in Schenker’s article Eine Rettung der klassischen Musik-Texte, Der Kunstwart vol. 42, No. 6 (March 1929). allerhand Beispiele zum Vortrag: Mozart Rondo Am, Schubert Sonate Bd; zeige den Abstand vom Facsimile u. Peters-Ausgabe im Menuett Hm von Schubert.
7. Bild-Korrektur des Finale abgeschlossen, zurück zum Scherzo.

17. Zeige Dunns Ornamentik,Petrie Dunn, Ornamentation in the Works of Chopin (London: Novello, 1921). den Sonderabdruck von Souchay;Marc-Andre Souchay, Das Thema in der Fuge Bachs (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1928); reprinted from the 1927 Bach-Jahrbuch. Chopin Etude op. 10III, Linie korrigirt.

21. Eintragungen
aus der rev. Abschrift, 2., 3., 4. Satz abgeschlossen; empfehle den Aufsatz von Landshoff in der „Musik“ u. das Selbst-Interview von Schönberg in der D.A.Z..Arnold Schoenberg, Interview mit mir selbst, Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung, December 16, 1928. -- Diary Nov 14: “An issue of Die Musik purchased, containing an article by Landshoff and one on Brahms's Violin Concerto.” Ludwig Landshoff, Die Aufführungspraxis Bachscher Chorwerke, Die Musik, xxi/2 (November 1928), 81–97
24. XII.(!!) Vortrag des 2. u. 3. Satzes der Sinfonie.

31. Vortrag des Finale; Anmerkungen zum Vortrag von Beethovens II. Sinfonie (gegen Spörr 30. XII).On December 30, Austrian Radio (RAVAG) broadcast a concert given by the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra under Martin Spörr, which concluded with a performance of Beethoven’s Second Symphony.

4. I. Auf die Ornamentik bezügliche Fragen aus Haydn-Sonaten, namentlich über den Doppelschlag von unten; über den Widerspruch in der Notierung von hairpin crescendo and decrescendo signs in Schubert Sinfonie Bd, 1. Satz; Haydn Sinfonie Ddur begonnen.Schenker’s diary (Dec 22) indicates that the Haydn symphony project had already been agreed some time before: “I work on Haydn Symphony in D major (Albersheim).” – Undated sketches of graphs for the symphony are preserved as OC 35/283 and 38/162 (first movement), and 35/302 (second movement).

7. Chopin Etude op. 10XII, Facsimile gezeigt; zum Vortrag von Beethoven Klavier-Konzert Cdur (Wang).Diary Jan 6, 1929: “Radio, 11 o'clock (Konrad): Brahms, Academic Festival Overture; Beethoven, Piano Concerto (Wang); Bruckner's Fourth.” – Stella Wang (1895–1974), Austrian pianist, for a time a pupil of Schenker’s friend Moriz Violin.
11. Winke zu Brahms Klavier-Violin-Sonate op. 78; für eine Geburtstagfeier in Köln.
21. Ich spiele Händel Suite No 2, 1. Satz, aus op. 13 von Beethoven das Adagio usw.
25. I. Haydn Abschluß des 1. Satzes, Vortrag.

28. Pedalstudien; bespreche Vrieslanders Korrektur zu Chopin Etude; Ornamentik in Haydn Sonate Edur bei Moscheles u. Päsler.Diary Jan 3, 1929: “Work on correcting the Schubert essay. — Haydn-Päsler arrives.” – This probably refers to Karl Päsler’s three-volume edition of Haydn’s keyboard sonatas, published by Breitkopf & Härtel c. 1918. Ignaz Moscheles prepared editions of eighteen sonatas, published around 1850 in Stuttgart by Eduard Hallberger and including Hob. XVI:31 in E major. — Diary Jan 28: “Albersheim inquires about my library, and about the publisher.”
1. II. Haydn: das Bild des Andante.Diary Jan 27: “after dinner, I work on the symphony by Haydn (for Albersheim).”

8. Zeige Hobokens Marsch u. Brünauers Klavierstück.Diary Feb 1: “Hoboken brings his march and two earlier compositions.” – Jan 29, 1929: “I show [Hoboken] Brünauer's composition; he replies: ‘I too have a march, for piano four hands.’" – Diary Feb 6: “Correction of Hoboken's and Brünauer's compositions.”
11. Haydn: Finale; nimmt Urlaub bis 1. März.Diary Feb 10: “In the evening, I work on Haydn (for Albersheim).” — Diary Feb 11: “Haydn for Albersheim finished – he is travelling to the Paznaun Valley!”
4. III. Haydn abgeschlossen, einschließlich des Vortrags.Diary Feb 24: “8:30 to 10:45 and 2 to 3:15, fair copy of Haydn's Finale (for Albersheim).”

8. Mozart Sinfonie Esdur begonnen.Diary Feb 12: “Rush to complete the first movement; Lie-Liechen following me with the fair copy on account of the necessity of making a start on Mozart's Symphony in E while Albersheim is on a short skiing holiday.”

11. Beratung zur Berufswahl.Diary March 11: “Albersheim asks my advice concerning choice of profession! He would like to stay in Vienna, conducting, teaching, or working for the Archive! He says that Hupka's position is almost hopeless: he is unable to gain any position. That reminds me of Hupka's naively stupid remark, when he once spent an evening with us: that my work was ‘hopeless’!”
15. Bach zweistimmige Invention Cdur, Bild korrigirt.

18. Bemerkungen zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der Jupiter-Sinfonie, in Handschrift u. Partitur verglichen.The program of the Vienna Philharmonic’s seventh subscription concert of the 1928/29 season comprised the “Jupiter” Symphony, Ernst Bloch’s Shelomo for cello and orchestra, and Brahms’s Fourth Symphony. A facsimile edition of the symphony was published by Universal Edition, Vienna, in 1923.

8. Gespräch; Verlobung, Pläne;Diary April 8: “Albersheim [...] mentions his engagement to Miss Halden. He says that they will rent a small apartment, that they both want to teach; he would very much welcome the founding of a publishing house by Hoboken at which he might find a position.” zeigt den Versuch einer Darstellung der Jupiter-Sinfonie.

15. Zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der IX. Sinfonie.This note, also repeated in Angi Elias’s lesson notes, may refer to a recollection of a performance of the Ninth Symphony by Furtwängler, or to the composer’s remarks about his approach to the work. He is not known to have performed the work in early 1929.

19. Zeige die Antwort der Baronesse FischerDiary April 15: “From Albersheim (express postcard): he asks for the address of Baroness Fischer. — To him, the address. — To Baroness Fischer (express letter): I say that Albersheim will be in touch.” — Diary April 26: “To Baroness Fischer (letter): Albersheim will delay the examination, because he – does not need it!”
u. Weisse; er weicht einer Prüfung noch aus.
22. Bild der Fuge aus Händel Suite.
29. Abschluß der Fugen-Korrektur; Chopin Prélude, Bild korrigirt.

6. Mozart Sinfonie abgeschlossen; Händel Suite II: Diminution im 2. Adagio; über den Unterschied von Händel u. Bach; über die Neigung Mozarts zu Dehnungen bei Gelegenheit von 3–3, bei IV7/3–V; Neigung zu Mischungen; Neigung zu Rhetorik bei Haydn; S. Bach vergleiche ich seiner Eindringlichkeit wegen mit der Therese von KonnersreuthTherese Naumann (1898–1962), German mystic who was born and spent her entire life in the Bavarian village of Konnersreuth. Her claims to have been cured of blindness and appendicitis by fervent prayer, and to have received the stigmata (the wounds that Christ suffered before his death) every Friday, made her a sensational figure in the 1920s. – auch Bach empfand alle Male Christi an sich, anders als Händel, der ganz in der Welt aufging; Bach: Gründer u. Zusammenhalter einer Familie, er begräbt Kinder, nimmt an Leichenbegängnissen anderer Teil als Kantor, in allen Prüfungen ganz Händel entgegengesetzt. Dieser, Opern-Unterneh-
-mer, macht Geschäftsreisen, feiert Helden, nicht Christus in Passionen, macht einige Konkurse durch, geht in einen Badeort! – Mozart Trio GdurOf Mozart’s two G major piano trios, K. 496 has a finale in the form of theme and variations, with coda.: eine klavier-technisch schwierige Stelle im Andante; Trio Gd letzter Satz: über die Variation Gmoll u. den Schluß, s. bei Brahms Schluß des Gdur Quintetts.

10. V. Brahms Rhapsodie Hm, neu.Diary May 5: “Fair copy of Brahms's Rhapsody in B minor (for Albersheim and Brünauer).” – Undated notes and a sketch for a graph of this work for Brünauer are preserved at OC 38/73 and other materials elsewhere in OC.
13. Fragen zu Tw. IV., Beispiele aus Händel, Mozart, Beethoven: ob oder ?Diary May 23: “I [answer] questions about the Tonwille 4 from Albersheim.”

24. Brahms op. 118 119 III Cdur, Linie korrigirt; zu Toscaninis Vortrag der Luzia; über die Unmöglichkeit Donizetti zu retten wegen seines Basses, der keine kontrapunktischen Prolongationen aufweist, vgl. Gluck, überhaupt die italienische u. französische Oper – oder den Jazz von heute. Nun ist aber die Musik im Abendland seit langem ein kontrapunktischer Satz bei dem auch der Baß wie eine Oberstimme
sich beträgt. Die abendländische Musik wird keine Erneuerung erfahren, bis sie nicht wieder zum Merkmal ihrer Geburt u. Frühzeit zurückkehrt, zum kontrapunktisch gehaltenen Außensatz. Ueber dem Unterschied von Rhythmik u. Metrik; über den Unterschied von „Technik“ u. wirklicher Technik. A. überrascht mich mit der Frage nach dem Gesetz vom Kopfton eines Zuges (!!)
27. Schnellfeuer von Fragen: aus der Instrumenten-Tabelle, über legato u. non legato bei Händel.

31. Ueberbringt einen Gruß von Rosé „mit besonderer Hochachtung“, ich sei mit dem älteren Bruder befreundet gewesen!Diary May 31: “Albersheim brings me greetings from Arnold Rosé, greetings of special esteem; he says that I had become a friend of his elder brother.” – Schenker himself confirms that he was “very good friends” with Alexander Rosé. Ueber den Unterschied von klassich u. romantisch in Musik, Malerei u. Architektur. Spielt die Händel-Fuge Fdur recht gut vor – ich korrigire Vortragsbemerkungen. Brahms–Haydn-Variationen, neu.Diary May 3: “From 2 to 4, I work on Brahms's Variations for Orchestra, as far as Variation 4 (for Albersheim).”

3. VI. Zur Methodik des Vor-
-trags; Erläuterung der Vortragsbezeichnung bei Brahms in der Sinfonie.Diary June 2: “I work for Albersheim.”
7. Chopin Sonate Fmoll Bmoll ,Diary June 4: “Fair copy of Chopin, Sonata in B minor, finale (Albersheim).” Finale, Bild korrigirt; über Zigeunermusik.
10. Fragen aus Chopin Polonaise, Prélude Fdur Bild korrigirt, Prélude Dm Bild korrigirt.
14. Fortsetzung u. Schluß der Brahms–Haydn Variationen.

21. Stellt in der letzten Stunde seine Braut vor – ich stelle ihm ein Zeugnis aus.Date supplied editorially on the basis of Schenker’s diary for June 21: “I attempt to get Albersheim to introduce his fiancée not after 1 o'clock, but actually earlier!”

tei:div.tei:ab: October 1: Mozart Eine kleine Nachtmusik; “Eroica” Symphony begun.
October 8: Mikulicz’s facsimile edition shown to him; the Minuet from Beethoven’s Op. 10, No. 3: passage with voice-exchange.
October 10: From Nottebohm’s sketchbook, sketches for the first movement, and how they are to be read.
October 19: First movement, correction of the graph completed.
October 22: Additional elucidations; entries from the revised copy of the score; performance, in broad outline.
October 26: Overture to A Midsummer Night’s Dream: graph of the Urlinie, unveiling of the deepest secrets of the parallelisms. Albersheim describes his visit to Nilius’s courses as a waste of time.
October 29: Second movement of the “Eroica” begun.
November 5: Further examination of the first movement, elucidation of several places in addition.

November 9: March from the music for A Midsummer Night’s Dream, graph of the Urlinie, and performance.
Observations on Hoesslins performance of Brahms’s First Symphony and Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique; Scherzo begun.
November 16: Graph of the fourth movement. Questions about Schubert’s Symphony in B major.
November 26: Questions about Schubert’s Rosamunde ballet music, the passages in B major and G minor; I show him Heck’s sketches for Beethoven’s Sixth Symphony, last movement.
November 30: Voice-leading line for Schubert’s C major Symphony, the passage in F major in the Andante; line for Chopin’s Nocturne in F major corrected; line for Bach’s Toccata in F major corrected.

December 3: Mendelssohn “Die Liebende schreibt,” voice-leading line corrected; all manner of examples on performance: Mozart Rondo in A minor, Schubert Sonata in B major; I show the how far the Peters edition diverges from the facsimile of the autograph manuscript of Schubert’s Minuet in B minor.
December 7: Corrections to the graph of the finale completed, back to the Scherzo.
December 17: I show him Dunn’s Ornamentation and the reprint of Souchay; Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 3, voice-leading line corrected.

December 21: Entries
made in the revised copy of the second, third and fourth movements completed; I recommend the article by Landshoff in Die Musik and Schoenberg’s interview with himself in the Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung.
December 24: Performance of the second and third movements of the Symphony.
December 31: Performance of the finale; remarks on the performance of Beethoven’s Second Symphony (in contrast to Spörr on December 30).

January 4: Questions about ornamentation in Haydn’s sonatas, especially the turn figure from below; on the contradiction in the notation of hairpin crescendo and decrescendo signs in Schubert’s Symphony in B major, first movement; Haydn’s Symphony in D major begun.
January 7: Facsimile of Chopin’s Etude Op. 10, No. 12 shown to him; on the performance of Beethoven’s Piano Concerto in C major (by Wang).
January 11: Suggestions about Brahms’s Sonata for Violin and Piano, Op. 78, for a birthday celebration in Cologne.
January 21: I play the first movement of Handel’s Suite No. 2 and the Adagio from Beethoven’s Op. 13, etc.
January 25: Haydn, completion of the first movement, performance.
January 28: Studies in pedaling; I discuss Vrieslander’s corrections to Chopin’s Etude; Ornamentation in Haydn’s Sonata in E major in the editions of Moscheles and Päsler.
February 1: Haydn: the graph of the Andante.
February 4: Haydn: the graph of the Minuet.
February 8: I show him Hoboken’s march and Brünauer’s piano piece.
February 11: Haydn: finale. He is going on holiday until March 1.
March 4: Haydn completed, inclusive of performance.
March 8: Mozart’s Symphony in E major begun.
March 11: Advice on choice of profession.
March 15: Bach’s Invention in C major: the graph corrected.
March 18: Observations on Furtwängler’s performance of the “Jupiter” Symphony, the manuscript compared with the score.
April 8: Conversation; engagement, plans; he shows me an attempt at a presentation of the “Jupiter” Symphony.
April 15: On Furtwängler’s performance of the Ninth Symphony.

April 19: I show him Baroness Fischer’s reply,
and Weisse’s; he is still avoiding an examination.
April 22: Graph of the fugue from Handel’s Suite.
April 29: Completion of the corrections to the fugue; Chopin Prelude, the graph corrected.
May 3: Questions about Schumann’s Symphonic Etudes.

May 6: Mozart’s symphony completed; Handel’s Suite No. 2: diminution in the second Adagio movement. On the difference between Handel and Bach. On Mozart’s penchant for expansions using 3–3, bei IV7/3–V; his penchant for mixtures of major and minor. Haydn’s penchant for rhetorical expression. I compare J. S. Bach, on account of his intensity, with Therese von Konnersreuth – Bach, too, found Christ at his side at all times, unlike Handel, who succeeded entirely as a man of the world. Bach: who creates a family and keeps it together, who buries children, who as cantor takes part in the funeral services, entirely the opposite to Handel in all his trials. The latter, opera entrepreneur,
takes business trips, celebrates heroes – not Christ in settings of the Passion – takes part in some competitions, goes to a bathing resort! – Mozart Trio in G major: a technically difficult passage in the Andante; last movement of the G major trio: on the G minor variation and the coda, cf. the close of Brahms’s Quintet in G major.
May 10: Brahms Rhapsody in B minor, new.
May 13: Questions about Der Tonwille issue 4, examples from Handel, Mozart, Beethoven: or ?

May 24: Brahms Op. 118 119 , No. 3, in C major, the voice-leading line corrected; on Toscanini’s performance of Lucia di Lammermoor; on the impossibility of rescuing Donizetti on account of his bass lines, which present no contrapuntal prolongations: compare Gluck, Italian and French opera in general – and today’s jazz. But for a long time, Western music has been a contrapuntal construction in which the bass, too, behaves as if it were an upper voice.
Western music will never experience regeneration until it returns to the sign of its birth and early times, to a contrapuntal outer-voice structure. On the difference between rhythm and meter; on the difference between “technique” and true technique. Albersheim surprises me with his question about the law of the primary tone of a linear progression. (!!)
May 27: Barrage of questions: from the Instrumentation Table, concerning legato and non legato in Handel.

May 31:He brings me a greeting from Rosé “with particular esteem,” as I have been a friend of his elder brother! On the difference between Classical and Romantic in music, painting, and architecture. He performs Handel’s fugue in F major very well – I correct the performance markings. Brahms’s Haydn Variations, new.
June 7: Chopin Sonata in F minor B minor , finale, graph corrected; on gypsy music.
June 10: Questions about a polonaise by Chopin; the graph of his Prelude in F major corrected, the graph of his Prelude in D minor corrected.
June 14: Continuation and conclusion of the Brahms Haydn Variations.
June 21: In the last lesson, he introduces me to his fiancée – I write a letter of reference for him.
